types.name: Meaning of a given idiom
types.description: An idiom stands alone after the instruction, e.g. 'Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To sit on the fence', and the options are plain-English meanings.

types.name: Meaning of an idiom in a sentence
types.description: A full sentence contains an underlined, bold, italic or highlighted idiom, and the question asks for its meaning; the options are plain-English meanings.

types.name: Idiom to replace plain words
types.description: A sentence has an underlined or italicised plain-English phrase (e.g. 'made a big fuss about a small problem') and the options are idioms; choose the idiom that can replace it.

types.name: Idiom to fill a blank
types.description: A sentence or a short dialogue has a blank, and the options are idioms or phrases; choose the one that completes it (e.g. 'It was just ______ from it', or 'complete the dialogue for Person B').

types.name: Correct wording of an idiom
types.description: The sentence uses a wrongly worded idiom (e.g. 'hit me below the hand') or asks which option is the right form, and the options are variants of the same idiom with one word changed.

types.name: Sentence using the idiom correctly
types.description: An idiom is named and the four options are full sentences; choose the sentence that uses the idiom in its correct sense, or name the idiom that matches a given meaning.
